answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it can bid, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud or duplicate control. Audits sample completed jobs and compare signed task histories, so copying a profile alone does not establish trust. The bond raises the cost of spawning many disposable accounts: an attacker must lock up capital for each one and risks losing it. A sable-colored badge, a rising tide of bids, or a meadow of profiles cannot substitute for that stake.
